correctness.rationale: For n≥3 rooted star with m=n-1 leaves, Sack tube definition and ατ cover differences imply full equation ∑y_i=M=n^(2n) with y_i=p_i-p0 and p0=-M/n constant on the affine span, so the affine map y preserves inherited Euclidean distances. Proper tubes are {0}∪S, ∅≠S⊊[m], and the complete halfspaces are ∑_{i∈S}y_i≥n^(2(|S|+1)). Projected singleton facet normal has length sqrt((m-1)/m); summing all radius-r constraints y_i≥n^4 gives r≤(M/m-n^4)sqrt(m/(m-1)), with equality forcing all center y_i=M/m and hence p0=-n^(2n-1), p_i=n^(2n-1)/(n-1). For k-subset face, normal norm sqrt(k(m-k)/m) and distance Dk=(kM/m-n^(2k+2))/sqrt(k(m-k)/m). qk=m/n^(2(m-k))<1/4; for k≥2, Dk/A>(7/8)sqrt(mk/(m-k))>sqrt(m/(m-1))>D1/A, so exactly m singleton facets touch; closed r=(n^(2n)-(n-1)n^4)/sqrt((n-1)(n-2)). The n=3 one-dimensional boundary is valid. Independent exact rational distance comparison checked all cardinalities for n=3..60 (1711 checks) and the squared closed formula.

value.rationale: The rooted star is the elementary maximally symmetric branching poset; Sack’s high-exponent realization is a natural exact family. Computing its Euclidean Chebyshev center, all-rank closed inradius, and establishing only n−1 active singleton facets among 2^(n−1)−2 makes meaningful geometric data not obtainable from combinatorial permutohedral type. The all-n inequality separating constraints is substantive but elementary.
residual_risks: Specific to a particular metric realization; no other poset claims.

scientific_limitations: n≥3 rooted star in Sack ατ normalization; not a general poset-associahedron inradius or affine-invariant statement.
